claim: The DNA unzipping technique can characterize the locations of a bound TF and a nucleosome simultaneously on long DNA templates to near base pair accuracy.
source: By examining the remodeling behavior upon encountering a bound TF, we determined that the relationship between TFs and nucleosome remodeling not only plays a critical role in nucleosome positioning, but also reveals a novel mechanism for how a TF can be dynamically recycled by nucleosome remodeling.
evidence: The manuscript describes using DNA unzipping to characterize positions and cites previous work demonstrating this capability.

claim: A TF serves as a major barrier to ISW1a remodeling and acts as a boundary for nucleosome repositioning.
source: We found that a TF serves as a major barrier to ISW1a remodeling, and acts as a boundary for nucleosome repositioning.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: SWI/SNF was able to slide a nucleosome past a TF with concurrent eviction of the TF from the DNA.
source: In contrast, SWI/SNF was able to slide a nucleosome past a TF, with concurrent eviction of the TF from the DNA, and the TF did not significantly impact the nucleosome positioning.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: The TF did not significantly impact nucleosome positioning by SWI/SNF.
source: In contrast, SWI/SNF was able to slide a nucleosome past a TF, with concurrent eviction of the TF from the DNA, and the TF did not significantly impact the nucleosome positioning.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing nucleosome distributions.

claim: The repression of transcription has often been correlated with the presence of nucleosomes.
source: Additionally, the repression of transcription has often been correlated with the presence of nucleosomes, the basic units of chromatin structure, in which histone–DNA interactions act as a barrier for RNA polymerase elongation along DNA (Li et al., 2007; Petesch and Lis, 2012; Teves et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Nucleosomes and TFs compete for binding to DNA.
source: Nucleosomes and TFs have been shown to compete for binding to DNA (Mirny, 2010; Moyle-Heyrman et al., 2011; Lickwar et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The competition between nucleosomes and TFs is based on the respective affinities of the TF and nucleosome for DNA, and depends upon DNA sequence, histone variants, and histone modifications.
source: This competition is based on the respective affinities of the TF and nucleosome for DNA, and depends upon DNA sequence, histone variants, and histone modifications.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Some TFs are known to recruit nucleosome remodelers.
source: Some TFs are known to recruit nucleosome remodelers.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Gal4DBD contains only the 147 amino acids of the N terminal domain of the Gal4 protein and does not have any known remodeler recruitment function.
source: Gal4DBD contains only the 147 amino acids of the N terminal domain of the Gal4 protein and does not have any known remodeler recruitment function.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system used.

claim: The equilibrium dissociation constant of Gal4DBD was determined to be 3.4 nM under the experimental conditions.
source: Under our experimental conditions, the equilibrium dissociation constant of Gal4DBD was determined to be 3.4 nM (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b.

claim: The bound Gal4DBD's lifetime was much longer than 1 hr.
source: In addition, the bound Gal4DBD's lifetime was much longer than 1 hr (the typical duration of a single molecule experiment) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3c.

claim: SWI/SNF family remodelers are known to be associated with nucleosome disruption.
source: SWI/SNF family remodelers are known to be associated with nucleosome disruption (Imbalzano et al., 1996; Logie and Peterson, 1997; Aoyagi et al., 2002) and transcriptional activation (Kwon et al., 1994; Hassan et al., 2001; Gkikopoulos et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF family remodelers are known to be associated with transcriptional activation.
source: SWI/SNF family remodelers are known to be associated with nucleosome disruption (Imbalzano et al., 1996; Logie and Peterson, 1997; Aoyagi et al., 2002) and transcriptional activation (Kwon et al., 1994; Hassan et al., 2001; Gkikopoulos et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISWI family remodelers have been shown to contribute to the formation of evenly spaced nucleosome arrays.
source: while ISWI family remodelers have been shown to contribute to the formation of evenly spaced nucleosome arrays (Tsukiyama et al., 1999; Fyodorov and Kadonaga, 2002; Lusser et al., 2005; Torigoe et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both SWI/SNF and ISWI remodeler families have been implicated in transcriptional activation and repression.
source: Despite these opposing characteristics, both remodeler families have been implicated in transcriptional activation and repression (Kwon et al., 1994; Moreira and Holmberg, 1999; Hassan et al., 2001; Martens and Winston, 2002; Whitehouse et al., 2007; Yadon et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Many ISWI remodelers have been shown to be sensitive to naked DNA segments flanking the nucleosome, preferentially sliding the nucleosome towards the longer segment of DNA.
source: On mononucleosome substrates, many ISWI remodelers have been shown to be sensitive to naked DNA segments flanking the nucleosome, preferentially sliding the nucleosome towards the longer segment of DNA (Yang et al., 2006; Blosser et al., 2009; Deindl et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF remodelers can shift a histone octamer up to 50 bp off the end of a short DNA fragment.
source: SWI/SNF remodelers, on the other hand, can shift a histone octamer up to 50 bp off the end of a short DNA fragment (Kassabov et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF remodelers have been found to shift one nucleosome onto another on dinucleosomal templates, indicating nucleosome disruption and eviction characteristics.
source: On dinucleosomal templates, SWI/SNF remodelers have been found to shift one nucleosome onto another, indicating nucleosome disruption and eviction characteristics of these remodelers (Engeholm et al., 2009; Dechassa et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Approximately 56% of nucleosomes remained at the original location after short remodeling time, suggesting a lack of remodeling.
source: During such a short remodeling time, ∼56% of nucleosomes pooled from measurements of multiple single molecules were found to remain at the original location, suggesting a lack of remodeling (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Of the remodeled nucleosomes, approximately 73% were remodeled only once and approximately 27% were remodeled more than once.
source: Of the remaining ∼45% of the nucleosomes that were remodeled, we estimate that ∼73% were remodeled only once and ∼27% were remodeled more than once, using a method we previously established (Shundrovsky et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on data analysis using a previously established method.

claim: In the absence of Gal4DBD, both ISW1a and SWI/SNF were able to move a nucleosome bi-directionally.
source: In the absence of Gal4DBD, although the nucleosome unzipping signature did not appear to be altered after remodeling by either ISW1a or SWI/SNF (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Shundrovsky et al., 2006), the positions of the nucleosomes were spread out from the original location. Both ISW1a and SWI/SNF were able to move a nucleosome bi-directionally (Figure 2B,C)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: In the presence of Gal4DBD, ISW1a moved the nucleosome away from Gal4DBD.
source: Interestingly, in the presence of Gal4DBD, ISW1a moved the nucleosome away from Gal4DBD (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The bound Gal4DBD affects the directionality of nucleosome movement by ISW1a and SWI/SNF differently: away from the TF for ISW1a and toward the TF for SWI/SNF.
source: Therefore, we conclude that the bound Gal4DBD affects the directionality of nucleosome movement by the two types of remodelers differently: away from the TF for ISW1a and toward the TF for SWI/SNF.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data from multiple templates with different orientations.

claim: The findings on TF directed ISW1a nucleosome remodeling are in agreement with a previous study that used NURF in the presence of Gal4DBD.
source: Our findings on the TF directed SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling are entirely novel; while our findings on the TF directed ISW1a nucleosome remodeling are in agreement with a previous study that used NURF (a homolog of ISWI complexes in Drosophila) in the presence of Gal4DBD (Kang et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim compares current findings to previous literature.

claim: The findings on TF directed SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling are entirely novel.
source: Our findings on the TF directed SWI/SNF nucleosome remodeling are entirely novel; while our findings on the TF directed ISW1a nucleosome remodeling are in agreement with a previous study that used NURF (a homolog of ISWI complexes in Drosophila) in the presence of Gal4DBD (Kang et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the manuscript.

claim: In the presence of Gal4DBD, nucleosomes remodeled by ISW1a were not able to pass the location of the Gal4DBD.
source: In contrast, in the presence of Gal4DBD, although nucleosomes were still moved away from the end of the template, they were not able to pass the location of the Gal4DBD (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The distribution of ISW1a-remodeled nucleosomes peaked at the midpoint between the Gal4 binding sequence and the 601NPE.
source: Instead, the distribution peaked at the midpoint between the Gal4 binding sequence and the 601NPE.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The dyad locations of the remodeled nucleosomes always nearly centered between the bound Gal4DBD and the template end.
source: After ISW1a remodeling in the presence of Gal4DBD, we found that the dyad locations of the remodeled nucleosomes always nearly centered between the bound Gal4DBD and the template end (Figure 3C; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Gal4DBD is a physical barrier for ISW1a mediated nucleosome remodeling.
source: These results demonstrate that Gal4DBD is a physical barrier for ISW1a mediated nucleosome remodeling and that ISW1a is able to use Gal4DBD as a reference point to reposition a nucleosome.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data showing nucleosome positioning relative to Gal4DBD.

claim: ISW1a is able to use Gal4DBD as a reference point to reposition a nucleosome.
source: These results demonstrate that Gal4DBD is a physical barrier for ISW1a mediated nucleosome remodeling and that ISW1a is able to use Gal4DBD as a reference point to reposition a nucleosome.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data showing nucleosome positioning relative to Gal4DBD.

claim: Deletion of ISWI in yeast disrupts nucleosome spacing.
source: Genome-wide nucleosome mapping in budding yeast revealed that deletion of ISWI in yeast disrupts nucleosome spacing (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011), suggesting that ISW1 remodelers are key players in generating evenly distributed nucleosomal arrays.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: ISW1 remodelers are key players in generating evenly distributed nucleosomal arrays.
source: Genome-wide nucleosome mapping in budding yeast revealed that deletion of ISWI in yeast disrupts nucleosome spacing (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011), suggesting that ISW1 remodelers are key players in generating evenly distributed nucleosomal arrays.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited literature.

claim: Certain DNA-binding factors located at the promoter region are responsible for nucleosome positioning.
source: In addition, several recent studies have shown that certain DNA-binding factors located at the promoter region are also responsible for nucleosome positioning (Whitehouse et al., 2007; Yadon et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2010; Bai et al., 2011; Hughes et al., 2012; Yen et al., 2012; Parikh and Kim, 2013; Struhl and Segal, 2013; Lieleg et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISW1a can potentially use a TF around the promoter region as a reference point to evenly position nucleosomes into the gene body.
source: Our finding that a bound Gal4DBD is a barrier to ISW1a now provides direct evidence to illustrate that ISW1a can potentially use a TF around the promoter region as a reference point to evenly position nucleosomes into the gene body.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings.

claim: Gal4DBD is not a physical barrier for SWI/SNF mediated nucleosome remodeling.
source: Both in the absence and presence of Gal4DBD, remodeled nucleosomes were detected on both sides of the original Gal4 binding position (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1). This indicates that Gal4DBD is not a physical barrier for SWI/SNF mediated nucleosome remodeling.
evidence: This conclusion is based on data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: SWI/SNF was able to move the nucleosome in such a way that the Gal4DBD was evicted from its binding sequence.
source: For the traces where nucleosomes were remodeled to the opposite side of the Gal4 sequence, we did not detect any Gal4DBD unzipping signature (Figure 4B; Figure 1—figure supplement 4). This indicates that SWI/SNF was able to move the nucleosome in such a way that the Gal4DBD was evicted from its binding sequence.
evidence: This conclusion is based on data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: SWI/SNF is unable to evict a bound Gal4DBD in the absence of a nucleosome.
source: Control experiments SWI/SNF is unable to evict a bound Gal4DBD in the absence of a nucleosome or in the absence of ATP (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by control experiment data.

claim: SWI/SNF is unable to evict a bound Gal4DBD in the absence of ATP.
source: Control experiments SWI/SNF is unable to evict a bound Gal4DBD in the absence of a nucleosome or in the absence of ATP (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by control experiment data.

claim: SWI/SNF remodeling is able to evict a bound TF and this eviction requires the presence of a nucleosome.
source: Therefore, we conclude that SWI/SNF remodeling is able to evict a bound TF and this eviction requires the presence of a nucleosome.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data including control experiments.

claim: SWI/SNF was shown to move one nucleosome to invade and eventually disrupt an adjacent nucleosome.
source: Previously, SWI/SNF was shown to move one nucleosome to invade and eventually disrupt an adjacent nucleosome (Dechassa et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: When ISW1a remodeled an end-positioned nucleosome on a template also containing a bound Lac repressor, the Lac repressor effectively dictated the position of the remodeled nucleosome.
source: When ISW1a remodeled an end-positioned nucleosome on a template also containing a bound Lac repressor, the Lac repressor effectively dictated the position of the remodeled nucleosome, with ISW1a centering the nucleosome on the DNA with the Lac repressor acting as a barrier (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SWI/SNF was able to slide a nucleosome in either direction, displacing the bound Lac repressor.
source: In contrast, SWI/SNF was able to slide a nucleosome in either direction, displacing the bound Lac repressor (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The mechanism of TF regulation by nucleosome remodeling is likely general without any specificity to a particular TF.
source: Therefore, we conclude that the mechanism of TF regulation by nucleosome remodeling is likely general without any specificity to a particular TF.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experiments with both Gal4DBD and Lac repressor showing similar results.

claim: SWI/SNF remodelers move nucleosomes toward the ends of a DNA template.
source: It has been widely acknowledged that SWI/SNF remodelers move nucleosomes toward the ends of a DNA template and ISWI remodelers move nucleosomes away from the ends of a DNA template (Stockdale et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2006; Zofall et al., 2006; Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISWI remodelers move nucleosomes away from the ends of a DNA template.
source: It has been widely acknowledged that SWI/SNF remodelers move nucleosomes toward the ends of a DNA template and ISWI remodelers move nucleosomes away from the ends of a DNA template (Stockdale et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2006; Zofall et al., 2006; Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ISW1a senses a bound TF as a boundary during nucleosome repositioning.
source: Here, we show that ISW1a senses a bound TF as a boundary during nucleosome repositioning, while SWI/SNF remodeling is unimpeded by the presence of a bound TF and is able to slide a nucleosome and evict the TF (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by experimental data.

claim: SWI/SNF remodeling is unimpeded by the presence of a bound TF and is able to slide a nucleosome and evict the TF.
source: Here, we show that ISW1a senses a bound TF as a boundary during nucleosome repositioning, while SWI/SNF remodeling is unimpeded by the presence of a bound TF and is able to slide a nucleosome and evict the TF (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by experimental data.

claim: The DNA-binding domain of ISW1a binds to approximately 29 bp of the extranucleosomal DNA.
source: Biochemical studies and the crystal structure of ISW1a indicate that the DNA-binding domain of ISW1a binds to ∼29 bp of the extranucleosomal DNA, which has been proposed to act as an anchor to pull the nucleosome towards ISW1a (Gangaraju and Bartholomew, 2007; Hauk and Bowman, 2011; Yamada et al., 2011; Hota et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The DNA-binding domain of ISW1a has been proposed to act as an anchor to pull the nucleosome towards ISW1a.
source: Biochemical studies and the crystal structure of ISW1a indicate that the DNA-binding domain of ISW1a binds to ∼29 bp of the extranucleosomal DNA, which has been proposed to act as an anchor to pull the nucleosome towards ISW1a (Gangaraju and Bartholomew, 2007; Hauk and Bowman, 2011; Yamada et al., 2011; Hota et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Snf6 subunit of SWI/SNF binds to approximately 15 bp of the extra-nucleosomal DNA.
source: In contrast, while it has been widely acknowledged that SWI/SNF does not require extra-nucleosomal DNA binding to remodel a nucleosome, cryo-EM and DNA-crosslinking experiments have shown that the Snf6 subunit of SWI/SNF binds to ∼15 bp of the extra-nucleosomal DNA and the rest of the SWI/SNF slides the nucleosome away from where the Snf6 subunit binds (Dechassa et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The Snf6 subunit has not been shown to be essential for remodeling.
source: Although the Snf6 subunit has not been shown to be essential for remodeling, it has DNA-binding affinity (Sengupta et al., 2001; Dechassa et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Snf6 subunit has DNA-binding affinity.
source: Although the Snf6 subunit has not been shown to be essential for remodeling, it has DNA-binding affinity (Sengupta et al., 2001; Dechassa et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF recruitment by the glucocorticoid receptor induced histone loss in nucleosomes and this was immediately followed by GR and SWI/SNF eviction from the template.
source: It has been previously shown that SWI/SNF recruitment by the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) induced histone loss in nucleosomes and this was immediately followed by GR and SWI/SNF eviction from the template (Nagaich et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the absence of remodeler recruitment, TF eviction via nucleosome remodeling can take place without substantial nucleosome loss.
source: Our current work demonstrates that, in the absence of remodeler recruitment, TF eviction via nucleosome remodeling can take place without substantial nucleosome loss.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings in this study.

claim: SWI/SNF can translocate along naked DNA.
source: Although SWI/SNF can translocate along naked DNA (Lia et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006; Sirinakis et al., 2011), raising the possibility for TF eviction solely by SWI/SNF, we found that in the absence of a nucleosome, SWI/SNF did not displace Gal4DBD from its binding site (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the absence of a nucleosome, SWI/SNF did not displace Gal4DBD from its binding site.
source: Although SWI/SNF can translocate along naked DNA (Lia et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2006; Sirinakis et al., 2011), raising the possibility for TF eviction solely by SWI/SNF, we found that in the absence of a nucleosome, SWI/SNF did not displace Gal4DBD from its binding site (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by control experiment data.

claim: SWI/SNF translocation alone is insufficient to displace a bound Gal4DBD and TF eviction requires nucleosome remodeling.
source: Thus, SWI/SNF translocation alone is insufficient to displace a bound Gal4DBD and TF eviction requires nucleosome remodeling.
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data from control experiments.

claim: Translocation by RSC was highly sensitive to a force in the DNA.
source: Previous work by Owen-Hughes and coworkers (Lia et al., 2006) found that translocation by RSC was highly sensitive to a force in the DNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A nucleosome regulates Gal4 binding not only by preventing Gal4 binding, but also by dramatically increasing the Gal4 dissociation rate from the DNA.
source: Indeed, a recent single molecule fluorescence study of Gal4 binding kinetics on nucleosomal DNA showed that a nucleosome regulates Gal4 binding not only by preventing Gal4 binding, but also by dramatically increasing the Gal 4 dissociation rate from the DNA (Luo et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF family remodelers are enriched upstream of the promoter regions in yeast.
source: Genome-wide mapping of yeast indicates that, apart from localizing to nucleosomes around transcription start sites, SWI/SNF family remodelers are also enriched upstream of the promoter regions (Yen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Brg1, Chd4, and Snf2h are highly enriched at the promoter and distal upstream regions in humans.
source: Genome-wide analysis of the locations of human chromatin remodelers also found that Brg1, Chd4, and Snf2h are highly enriched at the promoter and distal upstream regions (Morris et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SWI/SNF can slide nucleosomes to displace neighboring TFs around the promoter region.
source: Thus, although SWI/SNF alone does not possess any ability to remove TFs on its own, our work shows that SWI/SNF can slide nucleosomes to displace neighboring TFs around the promoter region, providing a mechanistic basis for dynamically clearing both nucleosomes and other bound factors upon SWI/SNF recruitment (Nagaich et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings in this study.

claim: Nucleosomes were assembled from purified HeLa histones onto the unzipping fragment by a salt dialysis method.
source: Nucleosomes were assembled from purified HeLa histones onto the unzipping fragment by a well-established salt dialysis method (Lee and Narlikar, 2001).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: yISW1a and ySWI/SNF were purified as previously described.
source: yISW1a and ySWI/SNF were purified as previously described (Gangaraju and Bartholomew, 2007; Dechassa et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used.

claim: yGal4DBD was purchased from Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Inc.
source: yGal4DBD was purchased from Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Inc., Dallas, TX.
evidence: This describes the source of materials used.

claim: The precision and accuracy of the experimental curves were improved to near base pair level by cross-correlation of regions.
source: The precision and accuracy of the experimental curves were improved to near base pair level by cross-correlation of regions immediately before the Gal4DBD disruption and after the nucleosome disruption, using methods as previously described (Hall et al., 2009; Li and Wang, 2012).
evidence: This describes the data analysis method used.

claim: Gal4DBD showed a distinct unzipping signature with a single force peak at 8 bp from the center of the consensus sequence.
source: Gal4DBD showed a distinct unzipping signature with a single force peak at 8 bp from the center of the consensus sequence (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3a), indicating the front end of the Gal4DBD footprint on the DNA.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3a.

claim: The disruption force peak for Gal4DBD was 18–20 pN, significantly larger than the baseline force of approximately 15 pN.
source: The disruption force peak was 18–20 pN, significantly larger than the baseline force of ∼15 pN.
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental data.

claim: The positioned nucleosome displayed a complex force signature with multiple force peaks and significantly greater overall force.
source: The positioned nucleosome displayed a much more complex force signature with multiple force peaks and a significantly greater overall force, reflecting the multiple finer and stronger histone–DNA interactions within a nucleosome (Shundrovsky et al., 2006; Hall et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental observations supported by citations.

claim: TF eviction is an intrinsic property of SWI/SNF remodeling and is independent of SWI/SNF recruitment.
source: Our study shows that TF eviction is an intrinsic property of SWI/SNF remodeling and is independent of SWI/SNF recruitment (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This conclusion is based on experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The results provide direct evidence for a novel mechanism for both nucleosome positioning regulation by bound TFs and TF regulation via dynamic repositioning of nucleosomes.
source: Our results provide direct evidence for a novel mechanism for both nucleosome positioning regulation by bound TFs and TF regulation via dynamic repositioning of nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion in the abstract.

claim: Proper transcriptional regulation depends upon transcription factors that bind to specific DNA-binding sites.
source: In eukaryotic cells, proper transcriptional regulation depends upon transcription factors (TFs) that bind to specific DNA-binding sites (Kadonaga, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Histone–DNA interactions act as a barrier for RNA polymerase elongation along DNA.
source: Additionally, the repression of transcription has often been correlated with the presence of nucleosomes, the basic units of chromatin structure, in which histone–DNA interactions act as a barrier for RNA polymerase elongation along DNA (Li et al., 2007; Petesch and Lis, 2012; Teves et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Understanding the relationship between TF binding and nucleosomes is essential in understanding gene expression and regulation.
source: Therefore, understanding the relationship between TF binding and nucleosomes is essential in understanding gene expression and regulation (Voss and Hager, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a motivation for the study supported by a citation.

claim: A nucleosome may be repositioned through the action of chromatin remodelers.
source: However, a nucleosome may also be repositioned through the action of chromatin remodelers, suggesting additional levels of transcription regulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Previous studies focused on how recruiting TFs affect the outcomes of nucleosome remodeling.
source: Previous earlier studies focused on how these recruiting TFs affect the outcomes of nucleosome remodeling (Nagaich et al., 2004; Boeger et al., 2008; Dechassa et al., 2010; Voss et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a summary of previous research supported by citations.

claim: It is unclear how TFs that do not recruit remodelers influence the chromatin landscape.
source: However, it is unclear how TFs that do not recruit remodelers influence the chromatin landscape.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that motivates the current study.

claim: Nucleosome remodeling may serve as an alternative mechanism to regulate transcription through its influence on a bound TF.
source: Thus, chromatin remodeling may serve as an alternative mechanism to regulate transcription through its influence on a bound TF, and a bound TF may dictate the location of a remodeled nucleosome.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: A bound TF may dictate the location of a remodeled nucleosome.
source: Thus, chromatin remodeling may serve as an alternative mechanism to regulate transcription through its influence on a bound TF, and a bound TF may dictate the location of a remodeled nucleosome.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: The DNA unzipping technique has been demonstrated to be a powerful single molecule technique for accurate and precise determination of positions and strengths of DNA–protein interactions.
source: We thus employed the DNA unzipping technique (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which has been demonstrated to be a powerful single molecule technique for accurate and precise determination of positions and strengths of DNA–protein interactions (Jiang et al., 2005; Shundrovsky et al., 2006; Hall et al., 2009; Jin et al., 2010; Dechassa et al., 2011; Li and Wang, 2012; Inman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The 601 nucleosome positioning sequence uniquely positions a nucleosome.
source: To evaluate the precision of this approach, we constructed a DNA template containing a single Gal4 sequence for binding to the Gal4 DNA-binding domain (Gal4DBD) and a single 601 nucleosome positioning sequence (601NPE) for uniquely positioning a nucleosome.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the 601 sequence.

claim: Both Gal4DBD and a nucleosome were readily detected above the baseline of the corresponding naked DNA in unzipping experiments.
source: The top trace of Figure 1 shows the result when the DNA template was unzipped starting from the Gal4 side. Both Gal4DBD (a single smaller peak) and a nucleosome (two clusters of larger peaks) were readily detected above the baseline of the corresponding naked DNA.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: It was often necessary to carry out unzipping experiments from both directions to detect both Gal4DBD and nucleosome.
source: The bottom trace shows the result when the DNA template was unzipped starting from the nucleosome side. Although the nucleosome unzipping signature was readily detectable, the unzipping signature of Gal4DBD was sometimes masked by that of the nucleosome. Therefore, it was often necessary to carry out unzipping experiments from both directions.
evidence: This is a methodological observation from the experiments.

claim: Analysis of unzipping signatures confirmed that unzipping mapped the position of the TF and the nucleosome to near base pair precision.
source: Analysis of these unzipping signatures confirmed that unzipping mapped the position of the TF and the nucleosome to near base pair precision ('Materials and methods'; Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Figure 1—figure supplement 3a; Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
